clue.text: Master I repeatedly disorientated, taking one subject after another

indicators.note: something disorientated is thrown out of its proper arrangement, so these letters are mixed up
repeatedly says the letter I is to be used twice over

explanation.surface: A schoolmaster loses his bearings while covering topic after topic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disorientated' rearranges MASTER plus I twice (MASTERII). SERIATIM is Latin for 'in a series', point by point.
explanation.definitionFit: Seriatim means taking items in order, point by point, which is dealing with each subject in turn.

clue.text: English trees rot

parts.note: the yew is a common evergreen tree
the ash is another familiar tree

explanation.surface: A dismissive verdict that English woodland is rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: The one word 'trees' supplies two trees in a row, YEW then ASH.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyewash is slang for nonsense or humbug, the same as calling something rot.

clue.text: Announce reduction for a change

indicators.note: for a change tells us to alter the order of the letters of the preceding word

explanation.surface: A notice proclaiming that prices will be cut, by way of variety.
explanation.definitionFit: To introduce a speaker or act is to announce them to an audience.

clue.text: Namely, how to deal with broken-down car

definitions.text: how to deal with broken-down car

explanation.definitionFit: 'To wit' is an old formula meaning that is to say; a broken-down car is dealt with by towing it away.

clue.text: Start afresh, and win hands down

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both to clear out everything old and begin again, and to win every prize or game in a contest.

clue.text: Musketeer briefly joins me for party

indicators.note: briefly asks us to shorten the word by cutting its final letter

parts.note: Athos is one of the Three Musketeers in Dumas's novel

explanation.surface: One of the Three Musketeers comes along with me to a celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: An at-home is a social gathering held in one's own house, a kind of informal reception.

clue.text: A rude dwelling, say, of an African type

indicators.note: say signals that we want a word that sounds like the phrase before it

parts.note: a shanty is a crude hut, so 'a rude dwelling' is 'a shanty'

explanation.surface: Describing a primitive hut as being in a particular African style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rude' here means crudely built, not impolite.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ashanti are a people of Ghana, so the word describes things belonging to that West African group.

clue.text: With difficulty carries sleeping policemen

explanation.definitionFit: To hump something is British slang for lugging it with effort; 'sleeping policemen' is the British name for speed bumps on a road.

clue.text: Mother hides a blemish .. using this?

definitions.text: Mother hides a blemish .. using this?

indicators.note: hides means the mother's word conceals the following pieces within it

parts.note: MA is a familiar word for mother
a scar is a mark or blemish on the skin

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a mother conceals a skin flaw with her make-up.
explanation.walkthrough: As a whole the clue pictures a woman using cosmetics to cover a flaw, making the clue a semi-&lit.
explanation.definitionFit: Mascara is eye make-up, a cosmetic a woman might use while making herself up.

clue.text: First defeat

explanation.definitionFit: The best is the top or foremost; to best an opponent is to beat them.

clue.text: Why mistake must be corrected for pupil

indicators.note: must be corrected implies the letters are wrongly ordered and need rearranging

explanation.surface: A teacher demands that a pupil put right a mistaken 'why'.
explanation.walkthrough: A WYKEHAMIST is a pupil or old boy of Winchester College, an English public school.
explanation.definitionFit: Wykehamists are students at Winchester College, founded by William of Wykeham.

clue.text: Warning to a disorganised travelling convoy

indicators.note: disorganised means the letters are put into disorder and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A warning sent to a straggling, chaotic convoy on the move.
explanation.definitionFit: A wagon train was a line of covered wagons travelling together, as in the American West.

clue.text: Photograph son having snooze

parts.note: a nap is a short snooze

explanation.surface: Taking a picture of a boy having a doze.
explanation.definitionFit: A snap is a casual snapshot, an informal picture taken with a camera.

clue.text: Ring in to secure call

indicators.note: in places the ring-shaped letter within the word for secure

parts.note: to secure a door is to shut it
O is shaped like a ring

explanation.surface: Telephoning a request to lock something up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring in' looks like a phone call; here 'Ring' is the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: A shout is a loud cry or call.

clue.text: American pilot, might one say?

indicators.note: might one say asks for a word that is pronounced like the description before it

parts.note: a pilot could be described as a plane's man

explanation.surface: Asking what one might call an airman from the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: A PLAINSMAN is a settler of the Great Plains, an American by type.
explanation.definitionFit: A plainsman is a frontier inhabitant of the North American prairies, a typically American figure.

clue.text: Clever clogs mixing salt with cream

indicators.note: mixing tells us to jumble the letters of the two words that follow

explanation.surface: A know-all in the kitchen combining salt and cream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clever clogs' is British slang for a know-all.
explanation.definitionFit: A smart alec is a cocky know-all, just what 'clever clogs' describes in British slang.

clue.text: Like governor's bad habit — knocked back the booze

parts.note: a vice is a bad habit

indicators.note: knocked back is read as turned backwards, not drunk

parts.note: lager is a common booze

explanation.surface: A governor's vice: he downed his beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked back' looks like drinking, but it reverses LAGER to give REGAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Viceregal describes things belonging to a viceroy, a governor ruling for a monarch.

clue.text: So-called dancer, as shown up in radio broadcast

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the scrambled one
broadcast means the letters are scattered and rearranged
shown up in a down clue means written upwards, so read backwards

explanation.surface: A dancer who, it is said, appeared on a radio programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shown up' looks like exposure, but in a down entry it means written upwards; 'broadcast' scrambles the radio. Isadora Duncan was the famous dancer known by her first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Isadora Duncan, pioneer of modern dance, was known by her first name, Isadora.

clue.text: Fellow supporting English team is very demanding

indicators.note: supporting in a down clue means placed beneath the other pieces

parts.note: XI is eleven, the size of a football or cricket team
a gent is a fellow or man

explanation.surface: A fan of the England side is very hard to please.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'supporting' puts GENT under E and XI.
explanation.definitionFit: Exigent means pressing or making great demands on someone.

clue.text: Temporarily interrupt personal assistant's employment

parts.note: employment of a thing is its use

explanation.surface: Briefly halting a secretary's job.
explanation.definitionFit: To pause something is to halt it for a while before carrying on.

clue.text: Soccer player in match

explanation.definitionFit: A striker is a forward in football; a striker is also something struck to make fire, like a match.

clue.text: Enthusiastic male joining conflict

parts.note: war is armed conflict

explanation.surface: A man keen to take part in battle.
explanation.definitionFit: A warm welcome is an eager, hearty one.

clue.text: Exotic palm, Eastern tree

indicators.note: exotic suggests something strange or unusual, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A foreign palm and an oriental tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The maple is a familiar deciduous tree, source of syrup.

clue.text: Officials in certain areas holding power

indicators.note: holding means the areas word contains the power letter

parts.note: sectors are defined areas or zones

explanation.surface: Bureaucrats in particular districts wielding authority.
explanation.definitionFit: Inspectors are officials who examine and check things on behalf of authority.

clue.text: Go into business? Not half!

indicators.note: not half means only half of the word is kept, its first part

explanation.surface: An exclamation agreeing heartily to start a company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half!' is British slang for 'absolutely'; here it keeps only the first half of ENTERPRISE.
explanation.definitionFit: To enter a room is to go into it.

clue.text: Express opinion about place given to English officers and crew

indicators.note: about means the opinion word goes round the other pieces

parts.note: to comment is to express an opinion

explanation.surface: Commenting on where English sailors are stationed.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's complement is its full company of officers and crew.

clue.text: Mere ingredients of 15 cornflakes

indicators.note: ingredients of means the answer lies among the letters of the following word

explanation.surface: Merely the contents of a cereal box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mere' looks like 'only', but it is a noun: a mere is a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A mere is a poetic or regional word for a small body of still water.

clue.text: Hollywood trial? Hot news

parts.note: Hollywood is in Los Angeles, abbreviated LA
a test is a trial

explanation.surface: A film-industry trial is the hottest story.
explanation.definitionFit: The latest is the most recent information, fresh news.

clue.text: Fish served with awfully ripe portion of fruit?

indicators.note: awfully suggests the letters are badly treated and must be rearranged

parts.note: a carp is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A fish dish accompanied by a badly overripe bit of fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: The pericarp is the wall of a fruit, the part around the seeds.
